draft.title: Connectives that build an argument
card: Connectives are words or phrases that link ideas. In an argument, they show how each idea relates to the one before it.
Adding
furthermore and in addition add another point in the same direction.
Opposing
in contrast, however and despite this set an idea against the last one or admit a point on the other side.
Result
therefore and as a result show that an idea follows from the one before.
draft.remember: Choose a connective to show whether an idea adds, opposes or follows.

a.q: Zoe writes: "The pool closed for repairs. ___, the swim team had nowhere to train." Which connective fits best?
opts: As a result
In contrast
However
Despite this
a.why: The team having nowhere to train follows from the pool closing, so as a result fits. In contrast and however would suggest the second idea opposes the first, which it does not.
a.clue: Does the second idea follow from the first?

b.q: Sam writes: "Cycling is cheap. ___, it keeps riders fit." Which connective fits, and what does it do?
opts: Furthermore, because it adds another point in support
In contrast, because it sets a point against cycling
Therefore, because it shows fitness causes low cost
Despite this, because it admits a point on the other side
b.why: Both sentences support cycling, so furthermore adds a second reason. Therefore is tempting, but being fit does not cause cycling to be cheap, so the result link is wrong.
b.clue: Both ideas point the same way.

b.best: Furthermore, because it adds another point in support

problems.detail: The Therefore option and the why both get the direction of the result link backwards. In 'Cycling is cheap. Therefore, it keeps riders fit', therefore would claim that being cheap causes fitness, not that fitness causes low cost. This could teach students the wrong direction for result connectives. The option should read something like 'Therefore, because it shows cheapness causes fitness', and the why should say that being cheap does not make riders fit.
